j8.1: Makes a query for each word: what the word is looking for in the others.
j8.2: Makes a key for each word: the word’s label, which other queries are compared against.
j8.3: Makes a value for each word: the content passed on if the word is selected.
j8.4: Merges the results from attention’s 32 heads into one vector that can be added to the notepad.
j8.5: Expands to 14,336 neurons and decides which ones to let through. Works like a dimmer.
j8.6: Also expands to 14,336, but carries the content the gate lets through.
j8.7: Squeezes back from 14,336 to 4096 numbers, so the result fits the notepad.
j8.8: Scales each dimension after the normalization before attention.
j8.9: The same thing before the MLP, with its own numbers.
j8.10: To scale: height = input, width = output.
j8.11: The norms are so small they only show as dashes.
j8.12: The nine parts in one layer add up to 218 million numbers. Almost 81% of them sit in the MLP’s three matrices.
j8.14: The vocabulary table at the start: 128,256 words × 4,096 numbers = 525 million. It is about as large as 2.4 layers.
j8.15: An equally large table at the end that turns the last vector into one score per word: another 525 million.
j8.16: One last normalization list with 4,096 numbers. Negligible, but included so the sum comes out exact.
j8.18: Every number is stored with 2 bytes in bf16. 8.03 billion × 2 bytes ≈ 16 GB, and that is how much GPU memory the weights require.
